newsitem.title: JAPAN: Weak stocks unlikely to spark financial worry - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Weak stocks unlikely to spark financial worry - MOF.

text.p: The recent decline in Tokyo share prices is unlikely to spark worries about Japan's financial system, a senior Ministry of Finance (MOF) official told Reuters on Wednesday.

The senior ministry official played down market concerns that Japanese financial institutions, already burdened with bad loans, will face problems in writing off their bad loans after the recent plunge in share prices. Stock price declines could trim unrealised profits from their share holdings.

"I don't think (recent stock declines) will lead to worries about the nation's financial system as a whole," the official said. He added that Japanese banks are likely to use their operating profits, rather than unrealised profits from their stock holdings, to carry out necessary bad loan write-offs.
Takai added that the unrealised profits would disappear for most of the banks if the key Nikkei average fell further to about 14,900.
He said he did not think falling stocks alone would directly hinder the banks' plans to write off their bad loans, but the decline would weaken their financial health.

"I see little direct impact from the weak stocks, but if the stock decline rekindles major banking worries here by weakening the banks' financial health, we might see a vicious circle (in which such worries invite a further slide in stock prices)," Takai said.
